title: Relative perfectness over a flat finitely presented algebra is equivalent to boundedness below plus boundedness of every residue field fibre

standard_prerequisites.name: An R-perfect complex has bounded tor dimension as a complex of R-modules, which gives the easy implication
standard_prerequisites.use: Proves one direction of the equivalence.

standard_prerequisites.name: A complex over a flat finitely presented algebra may be viewed as a complex over a polynomial algebra over the base, and pseudo-coherence and relative perfectness are unaffected by this change of algebra because the two have the same image over the base
standard_prerequisites.use: Reduces the general case of the statement to the case of a polynomial algebra over the base.

standard_prerequisites.name: For a flat local map whose fibre is regular of finite dimension, a pseudo-coherent complex whose derived fibre at the closed point is bounded below is perfect, and boundedness below of a pseudo-coherent complex is checked on localizations
standard_prerequisites.use: Gives perfectness of the localizations at primes of the algebra, whence perfectness of the complex itself.

core_obligations: Dispose of the easy implication: an R-perfect complex has bounded tor dimension over the base by definition, hence is bounded below and so are all its residue field fibres (proof lines 22215-22216).

For the converse, write the algebra as a quotient of a polynomial algebra, view the complex over that polynomial algebra and use the mootness statement to keep pseudo-coherence; observe that relative perfectness and the residue field fibres are unchanged, reducing to the case of a polynomial algebra over the base (proof lines 22218-22227).

In that case, take a prime of the algebra lying over a prime of the base and apply the local criterion for perfectness over a regular fibre using the assumption on the fibre at that prime, obtaining that the localization of the complex is perfect (proof lines 22229-22238).

Use boundedness below together with the stalk criterion for perfectness to conclude that the complex is perfect, and then apply the statement identifying perfect complexes with relatively perfect ones over the base to finish (proof lines 22238-22244).
proof_roadmap: One direction from bounded tor dimension of a relatively perfect complex (proof lines 22215-22216).
Reduce to a polynomial algebra over the base and keep relative perfectness and the fibres unchanged (proof lines 22218-22227).
Apply the local perfectness criterion fibrewise, then the stalk criterion and the identification with relative perfectness (proof lines 22229-22244).
difficulty_reason: The statement characterizes relative perfectness of a pseudo-coherent complex over a flat finitely presented algebra by two conditions: boundedness below of the complex and boundedness below of each of its residue field fibres over the base (statement lines 22204-22213). The easy direction is immediate from bounded tor dimension, while the converse requires reducing the algebra to a polynomial algebra over the base, invoking the local perfectness criterion over a regular fibre prime by prime, then the stalk criterion for perfectness and finally the identification of perfect complexes with relatively perfect ones (proof lines 22215-22244). The reduction and the two applications of the local criteria are the substance of the proof. The counted span refers four times to results of this chapter, all carried as navigation stubs.
